intro.data: Welcome. Everything here is built from two ideas. The rounded pills are THINGS (we call them objects). The boxes between them are PROCESSES that turn one thing into another — a process is a morphism. Drag from the Start into a machine, then into the Goal. Two machines fit; only one actually makes a clean table. Run it to see.
intro.alchemy: Welcome. Everything here is built from two ideas. The rounded pills are THINGS (objects). The boxes are PROCESSES that turn one thing into another — a process is a morphism. Drag from the Start into an apparatus, then into the Goal. Two fit; only one makes a pure ingot. Run it to see.
intro.spellcraft: Welcome. Everything here is built from two ideas. The rounded pills are THINGS (objects). The boxes are WORKINGS that turn one thing into another — a working is a morphism. Drag from the Start into a rune, then into the Goal. Two fit; only one makes a steady flame. Run it to see.
intro.abstract: Two ideas underlie everything. Pills are objects. Boxes are morphisms: processes A → B. Wire the input through a machine to the goal. Two are type-valid; only one produces the goal value.

afterSuccess.data: That arrow you drew is a morphism — a process from one object to another. Both machines were the same type (Raw → Clean), but they behaved differently. A process is defined by what it DOES, not just what it connects.
afterSuccess.alchemy: That arrow is a morphism — a process from one object to another. Both apparatuses were the same type, but behaved differently. A process is defined by what it DOES.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: That arrow is a morphism — a working from one object to another. Both runes were the same type, but behaved differently. A working is defined by what it DOES.
afterSuccess.abstract: The arrow is a morphism. Same-typed morphisms can behave differently; a morphism is defined by its action, not just its type.

reveal.summary: The things are objects; a process between them is a morphism (an arrow). Two morphisms A → B can still do different things.
reveal.programmerAnalogy: f: (input: A) => B — two functions with the same signature can compute different things.

intro.data: One process is rarely enough. The output of one machine can feed the input of the next — that chaining is called composition. Clean the data, THEN chart it. Wire Start → Parser → middle → Charter → Goal, then run a value all the way through.
intro.alchemy: One process is rarely enough. The output of one apparatus can feed the next — that chaining is composition. Refine the ore, THEN shape it. Wire Start → Smelter → middle → Toolsmith → Goal, then run a value through.
intro.spellcraft: One working is rarely enough. The output of one rune can feed the next — that chaining is composition. Tame the spark, THEN kindle it. Wire Start → Ignition → middle → Kindler → Goal, then run a value through.
intro.abstract: Compose two morphisms: the output of f feeds g. Wire A → f → B → g → C so the value flows the whole way.

afterSuccess.data: You composed two processes: Parser then Charter. The clean table that came out of the first machine became the input to the second. Written as one combined process, that is g ∘ f — "g after f".
afterSuccess.alchemy: You composed two processes: Smelter then Toolsmith. The ingot from the first fed the second. Combined, that is g ∘ f — "g after f".
afterSuccess.spellcraft: You composed two workings: Ignition then Kindler. The flame from the first fed the second. Combined, that is g ∘ f — "g after f".
afterSuccess.abstract: You composed g after f. The output of f became the input of g, giving one combined morphism g ∘ f : A → C.

reveal.summary: Composition chains processes: if f : A → B and g : B → C, then g ∘ f : A → C runs f, then g. The middle types must match.
reveal.programmerAnalogy: const gf = (x: A) => g(f(x)) — function composition.

intro.data: Every object has one special process that changes nothing: it takes a thing and hands back the very same thing. It's called the identity. Start and Goal are the SAME object here. One machine returns it untouched; the other quietly smudges it. Pick the one that truly leaves it unchanged, then run it.
intro.alchemy: Every object has one special process that changes nothing: it hands back the very same material. It's called the identity. Start and Goal are the SAME object. One apparatus returns it untouched; the other taints it. Pick the untouched one, then run it.
intro.spellcraft: Every object has one special working that changes nothing: it hands back the very same essence. It's called the identity. Start and Goal are the SAME object. One rune returns it untouched; the other warps it. Pick the untouched one, then run it.
intro.abstract: Every object A has an identity morphism id_A : A → A that returns its input unchanged. Start and Goal are the same A. Pick the morphism that truly leaves the value alone.

afterSuccess.data: Hold is the identity on this object: it returns exactly what it received. Smudge had the same type (Record → Record) but changed the value — so it is NOT an identity. Every object has exactly one identity.
afterSuccess.alchemy: Rest is the identity on this object: it returns exactly what it received. Taint had the same type but changed the sample — so it is NOT an identity. Every object has exactly one identity.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: Stillness is the identity on this object: it returns exactly what it received. Warp had the same type but changed the essence — so it is NOT an identity. Every object has exactly one identity.
afterSuccess.abstract: id_A returns its input unchanged. A same-typed self-loop that alters the value is not an identity. Each object has exactly one id_A.

reveal.summary: The identity id_A : A → A is the do-nothing process on an object. Composing with it changes nothing: f ∘ id = f = id ∘ f.
reveal.programmerAnalogy: const id = (x: A) => x — the identity function.

intro.data: Some processes can be perfectly undone. Encode the original, then decode it — and if you get the EXACT original back, the two processes are inverses and the objects are isomorphic ("the same up to renaming"). Two decoders are offered; only one restores the original exactly. Build the round trip Start → encode → decode → Goal and run it.
intro.alchemy: Some processes can be perfectly undone. Transmute the original, then revert it — if you get the EXACT original back, the two are inverses and the objects are isomorphic. Two reverters are offered; only one restores it exactly. Build the round trip and run it.
intro.spellcraft: Some workings can be perfectly undone. Seal the original, then unseal it — if you get the EXACT original back, the two are inverses and the objects are isomorphic. Two unsealings are offered; only one restores it exactly. Build the round trip and run it.
intro.abstract: An isomorphism f : A → B has an inverse g : B → A with g ∘ f = id_A. Build the round trip A → f → B → g → A; only the true inverse restores the original value.

goal.data: Make the round trip return the EXACT original — pick the decoder that truly inverts the encoder.
goal.alchemy: Make the round trip return the EXACT original — pick the reverter that truly inverts.
goal.spellcraft: Make the round trip return the EXACT original — pick the unsealing that truly inverts.
goal.abstract: Build g ∘ f = id_A with the true inverse g.

afterSuccess.data: Decode is the inverse of Encode: the round trip returned the EXACT original, so g ∘ f = id. Lossy Decode had the right type but corrupted the message, so it was not a true inverse. When a process has an inverse, it is an isomorphism, and its two objects are "the same up to renaming".
afterSuccess.alchemy: Revert is the inverse of Transmute: the round trip returned the EXACT original, so g ∘ f = id. Rough Revert had the right type but lost metal, so it was not a true inverse. A process with an inverse is an isomorphism.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: Unseal is the inverse of Seal: the round trip returned the EXACT original, so g ∘ f = id. Cracked Unseal had the right type but frayed the sigil, so it was not a true inverse. A working with an inverse is an isomorphism.
afterSuccess.abstract: g ∘ f = id_A, so g is the inverse of f and f is an isomorphism. A same-typed map that doesn't restore the value is not an inverse.

reveal.summary: If f : A → B has an inverse g : B → A with g ∘ f = id_A and f ∘ g = id_B, then f is an isomorphism and A ≅ B — the objects are interchangeable up to renaming.

intro.data: The last big idea: a functor lifts an ENTIRE world into another. On the right is the plain world — one Cleaner turning one record into one clean record. The Batch world holds many records at once. "Lifting" the Cleaner means finding the machine that cleans EVERY record in a batch. One machine does; the other crumples them. Lift it, then run a batch through.
intro.alchemy: The last big idea: a functor lifts an ENTIRE world into another. On the right is the plain world — one Smelter refining one ore. The Crate world holds many at once. "Lifting" the Smelter means finding the machine that refines EVERY ore in a crate. One does; the other crushes them. Lift it, then run a crate through.
intro.spellcraft: The last big idea: a functor lifts an ENTIRE world into another. On the right is the plain world — one Kindler turning one spark into one flame. The Flock world holds many at once. "Lifting" Kindler means finding the working that kindles EVERY spark in a flock. One does; the other smothers them. Lift it, then run a flock through.
intro.abstract: A functor F lifts a whole world into another: each object A to F(A), each morphism f to F(f) doing the same job in the new world. Build F(f) : F(A) → F(B). The impostor is not the lift of f.

goal.data: Turn a batch of raw records into a batch of clean records — by lifting the Cleaner.
goal.alchemy: Turn a crate of ore into a crate of ingots — by lifting the Smelter.
goal.spellcraft: Turn a flock of sparks into a flock of flames — by lifting Kindler.
goal.abstract: Take F(A) to F(B) with F(f).

afterSuccess.data: You lifted the Cleaner into the Batch world: F(f) cleans every record, doing to a whole batch what the plain Cleaner did to one. That assignment — each type A to F(A), each process f to F(f) — is a functor. (You've now met every core idea: objects, morphisms, composition, identity, isomorphism, and functors. Onward!)
afterSuccess.alchemy: You lifted the Smelter into the Crate world: F(f) refines every ore. Each type A to F(A), each process f to F(f) — that is a functor. You've now met every core idea. Onward!
afterSuccess.spellcraft: You lifted Kindler into the Flock world: F(f) kindles every spark. Each essence A to F(A), each working f to F(f) — that is a functor. You've now met every core idea. Onward!
afterSuccess.abstract: You built F(f), the lift of f. Sending each object A to F(A) and each morphism f to F(f) is a functor. You've now met objects, morphisms, composition, identity, isomorphism, and functors.

reveal.summary: A functor F : C → D lifts a whole category into another: each object A to F(A), each morphism f : A → B to F(f) : F(A) → F(B) doing the same job in the new world (preserving identities and composition).
reveal.moreFormal: List, Optional, and Batch are functors: F(A) wraps A, and F(f) = "apply f inside". Chapter 4 explores the laws F(id) = id and F(g ∘ f) = F(g) ∘ F(f).
reveal.programmerAnalogy: List is a functor: List<A>, and map(f): List<A> => List<B>.
